chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Ibn Abi Ya'fur said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man becomes junub in the month of Ramadan, then he wakes up, then he sleeps until morning. He said: He completes his day and makes up one other day. If he does not wake up until morning, he completes his day and it is valid for him.

key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: becomes junub (enters state of major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting if one becomes junub in Ramadan and sleeps until Fajr?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar highlights the juristic distinction between waking up in a state of major impurity (junub) before Fajr versus remaining asleep until the call to prayer, a key point of discussion among Shia scholars regarding the validity of the day's fast. It underscores the principle that the state of impurity at the time of Fajr does not invalidate the fast if one was fasting during the day, reflecting the Shia view that 'waking up junub' is not a nullifier of fasting. This ruling is often contrasted with the Hanafi view, which requires making up the day if one remains junub until Fajr, illustrating the diversity in fiqh methodologies.
